validated_results.title: Dietary patterns, polygenic risk, and kidney cancer incidence: a UK Biobank cohort study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective UK Biobank cohort reporting an adjusted hazard ratio for DASH dietary pattern adherence and incident kidney cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Higher versus lower DASH dietary pattern score
extraction.population: UK Biobank participants who completed at least two 24-hour dietary recalls

sample_size.excerpt: We conducted a prospective cohort study involving 113,594 participants from the UK Biobank who completed at least two 24-hour dietary recalls, and adherence to four dietary patterns (Alternate Mediterranean Index (aMED), Alternative Healthy Eating Index 2010 (AHEI), dietary approaches to stop hypertension (DASH), and dietary inflammatory index (DII)) was assessed.

cases.excerpt: During a median follow-up of 11.44 years, 425 participants developed kidney cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: Higher aMED (HR = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.54-0.94) and DASH (HR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.49-0.90) were associated with reduced risk of kidney cancer, while higher DII was associated with increased risk (HR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.02-1.79). Moreover, participants with high genetic risk combined with low aMED, AHEI and DASH scores or high DII score presented the highest kidney cancer risk.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Higher aMED (HR = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.54-0.94) and DASH (HR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.49-0.90) were associated with reduced risk of kidney cancer, while higher DII was associated with increased risk (HR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.02-1.79).

comparison.excerpt: Higher aMED (HR = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.54-0.94) and DASH (HR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.49-0.90) were associated with reduced risk
